# Solo performance: implementation and remaining qualification

Updated **19 October 2026, 01:15 Berlin (18 October 23:15 UTC)**. This status supersedes historical Current/Latest labels below; original evidence and failed outcomes remain unchanged.

**Core fixes are published; the plan is not complete.** Original [#1544](https://github.com/mekhovov/revealline/pull/1544) is merged. Main remains dd337c8; the latest verified public build is e440030. Soundtrack #1619, Missions #1620 and trace #1621 passed their final release gates and await the merge controller. Demo #1628 passed focused aggregation and awaits its final gate. New artwork and trail improvements are pushed to held branches. A further source review found a concrete main-thread MP3 scan before the existing worker; that gap is now a priority repair. No new native or physical-device pass is claimed.

Reviewed binary-artwork and trail-allocation changes are held. | Admit the narrow worker repair and prepared changes through source/build gates; verify current/next music, cold/warm Start and long cuts on the final package. |
| P1 — Attribution and resources | Historical trace is incomplete; Demo/Retry native resource exits remain failed. | Run the original trace-v2 after #1621, before adapter changes; run changed Demo cycles; then admit bounded Retry heap evidence and investigate actual retainers. |

Physical devices are unavailable; local work remains read-only. | Freeze the combined package, run equivalent repeated correctness/performance/raster/sustained scenarios, and qualify iPhone 17 Pro Safari and Steam Deck OLED Chrome when available. |

**Phase status.** Phase 0 diagnostics and phase segmentation are implemented, but complete attribution is pending. Phase 1 timing, lazy validation and direct mission identity are implemented; new trail changes still require strict replay validation. Phase 2 preparation/admission and worker infrastructure are implemented, but the newly found acquisition scan bypass must be repaired. Phase 3 rendering/HUD/cache/quality changes are implemented; final raster and performance gates remain open. Phase 4 is partly delivered: binary artwork and deferred menu/authoring work are not yet merged, while large-profile/save profiling remains open. Phase 5 is incomplete. “Source-reviewed,” “tests passed,” “merged,” “published” and “native-qualified” are distinct states.

**Release cohort.** Counts are overlapping scoped suites, not a unique whole-app test total. All ready heads remain unchanged.

**Release order and queue.** All seven trusted policy files match main across the four ready heads, and current-main compatibility checks found no required blanket rebase. The controller is the merge authority. Its queued completion events have not yet replaced old draft decisions; no policy refusal or environment-approval blocker was found. All superseded plan runs are terminal, so there is no obsolete documentation run left to cancel. Do not add duplicate triggers while completion events remain pending. If they all settle without reconciliation, use one normal rerun of an existing controller event with unchanged guards.

Keep #1654 draft through #1619/#1620/#1621/#1628, the P0 public observation and admission/merge of #1674/#1675/#1676. Then reconcile #1654 against fresh main and run its checks once. Its trusted-policy change must not invalidate the current admitted receipts mid-sequence. First CI for the held heap/overhead/artwork/trail and new worker repair follows that finite policy step; these items do not extend the hold indefinitely. New drafts remain unmerged through the P0 observation window.

**Publication.** [e440 publisher 39166266155](https://github.com/mekhovov/revealline/actions/runs/39166266155) completed successfully at 22:54:32 UTC, including final verification. Independent readback matched public identity before/after and 20 selected files against package metadata. Its selected-practice result checked zero optional practice payloads; it is not practice gameplay evidence. [dd337 publisher 39168765766](https://github.com/mekhovov/revealline/actions/runs/39168765766) has a queued build. Public bytes and successful deployment do not replace gameplay checks.

**Source review findings.** A cold official/bundled soundtrack is synchronously inspected in `soundtrack-source.mjs` before `soundtrack-player.mjs` reaches its worker; next-track preparation can take this path during active play. This is a confirmed reachable cost, not proof it caused the reported hitches. The repair uses the existing transport inspector and privately reuses successful facts only for the exact same immutable Blob within that one load. Both pinned-integrity comparisons remain, and other readers still receive normal validation. The [File API](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob) defines Blob bytes as immutable; this does not justify trusting arbitrary caller metadata.

The wider audio audit found bounded but unscheduled cold recorded-speech parsing during play. Current misses immediately show captions and only prepare a future occurrence; warmup is opportunistic and Start does not await it. At the existing two MiB input cap, a valid WAV can still contain 262,140 chunks. Keep cold-demand speech profiling explicit before changing cue readiness or adding another worker. Demo's explicit Play Style action can prepare a complete saved MP3 library while Demo runs; profile this separately from Main's current/next transport. Other inspected Main MP3 scans are explicit paused Studio/import/export or separately owned offline work.

Targeted Canvas2D review found display/scratch ownership, paused restoration, cache rebuilding and explicit Resume controls already present, with source tests for multiple lost surfaces and pending-readiness cancellation. Offline observation detaches independently; only explicit owned cancellation requests worker pause. No additional renderer/offline change was justified by this review, and native recovery still needs qualification.

The save/export audit preserves Solo's intentional readable display versus compact download and its existing recorded-actor/raw ownership behavior. A proposed shared terminal optimization was not implemented because that helper serves Team/Versus and would not close Solo's long-recording item. Paused Solo backup conversion and Team/Versus duplicate serialization remain P2 profiling candidates. Proof validation and durable-save guarantees stay intact.

**Historical failures and attribution.** Normal published smoke on 461 still failed: WebKit reached Solo Start/Pause/Resume then stalled at Missions; Chromium failed required-module boot on a 503. Earlier Team preparation failure, Demo geometry retention, Retry/resource thresholds, sustained cadence misses, touch/Next qualification and incomplete overhead/journal rows remain open. Source passes do not erase those outcomes. The old 9d trace lacks its end marker and reports data loss. Its long tasks include native/microtask/IndexedDB work, while the largest retained JavaScript FunctionCall is 17.406 ms. Eight long compositor readbacks occur before the actual Start click. The exact harness contains no screenshot or explicit pixel-readback call, but indirect automation/layout/compositor effects are still possible. Do not attribute the enclosing tasks to tiny adjacent callbacks or claim a complete-window pass.

**Measurement and native sequencing.** Run one original trace-v2 after #1621 and before changing shared adapters: existing frame-trace lane, unchanged historical package/protocol and bounded evidence owners. Recheck artifact availability, exact workflow/source and duplicate runs immediately before dispatch. The historical package expires 25 October at 11:44 UTC. For public Missions, hold our release intents during both engines, verify exact public identity and use the existing 570/600/720-second bounds without automatic retries. Backup is a separate scenario.

Minimum observed timer increments do not establish maximum duration error. Exact-source review found Chromium randomized coarsening and WebKit millisecond flooring; actual executable/configuration binding remains open. More repetitions cannot remove systematic timer uncertainty, and raw trace clocks have observer costs. The [High Resolution Time specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/hr-time-3/#dfn-coarsen-time) permits implementation-defined coarsening/jitter. Keep the 5% per-frame p95 target; do not substitute block averages or label unresolved rows as passes.

**Evidence retention.** [Index 97dc587](https://github.com/mekhovov/revealline/blob/97dc587588f4521ccfc81fdd0bb2812a805c0173/docs/performance/retained-audits/20261018/index.json) anchors 150 verified records, preserving every earlier entry. Index: 34,616 bytes, SHA256 2f50fcc2ccd1aaa7b34ca90d314467dddb2e33b31835b27b25a367ebfe8ac154. It includes final release/publication receipts, source proposals, independent reviews and held branch identities. Large build archives remain remote. [Previous plan snapshot](https://github.com/mekhovov/revealline/blob/153b13445a5c32f3aa6b63113b56fb3c11a008cc/docs/performance/solo-performance-followup-plan.md) preserves the preceding state. New renderer/offline, export-scope and media-caller audits are awaiting the next evidence-index batch; they are source reviews, not new qualification results.

**Estimates and external limits.** Hosted jobs are queued without assigned runners; their scheduling cause and completion ETA are not established. There is no reliable overall release ETA. After admission/publication, the public diagnostic has a maximum 12-minute outer owner per engine; original trace keeps its existing 75-minute helper/130-minute job bounds, not promised durations. Final sustained testing alone requires at least six aggregate browser-hours for three matched 30-minute baseline/candidate runs in two engines, plus other scenarios and repair time. Physical qualification needs approximately 1–3 hours per device when available; there is no device-availability ETA. Local disk stability, Cocoa test ownership and permission to publish private media remain separate limits. Do not mark the plan complete while required native or physical checks are failed, unavailable or unresolved.
